```{r library_etc, warning=FALSE}
# Source alosa functions
```

# Data - Load
```{r get_MARFIS_data}
# This is where we store the MARFIS pulls:
# R:/Science/Population Ecology Division/DFD/Alosa/MARFISSCI/Old pulls/marfis_pull.Rdata

# This function checks to see when the last pull was and asks if you'd like to
# update the pull. It then loads the MARFIS data without changing anything.
# If you decide to do a new MARFIS pull and there are new additions to the db
# that were not in the last pull, you will be prompted to make changes to the
# Master Rivername Database. This is located on the R drive here:'
# R:/Science/Population Ecology Division/DFD/Alosa/MARFISSCI/MASTER_RIVERNAME_DATABASE.csv
#source(here("other_functions", "pull_marfis_data.R"))

# You don't always have to pull the MARFIS data when working with it, that just
# updates the copy of the data we have to the most up to date version. If you 
# want to load MARFIS data that already exist, just load it from here:
load("R:/Science/Population Ecology Division/DFD/Alosa/MARFISSCI/Old pulls/marfis_pull.Rdata")
```

# Data - Cleaning
```{r, warning=FALSE}
# The function we use to clean the data is currently located here:

# "R:/Science/Population Ecology Division/DFD/Alosa/MARFISSCI/MARFIS.error.cleaner.R"

# This function contains data which CANNOT be stored on the unit github page
# because it contains information that ostensibly could be used to glean how
# much someone is earning, so we store it on the R drive, which seems a bit
# extra. However, this is the rule (for now)
source("R:/Science/Population Ecology Division/DFD/Alosa/MARFISSCI/MARFIS_error_cleaner.R")

df <- marfis_error_cleaner(
  catch = catch,
  years = "all",
  convert_to_kgs = TRUE,
  tidy_data = TRUE,
  correct_eel_pot = TRUE,
  unknown_rivers_are_na = TRUE,
  unknown_gear_are_na = TRUE
  )
```

# Data - Exploration
```{r}

# Get number of observations
df |> 
  filter(RIVERNAME_CLEANED == "TUSKET") |> 
  filter(YEAR %in% c(2020:2025)) |> 
  mutate(YEAR = as.factor(YEAR)) |>
  group_by(YEAR, LICENCE_ID) |> 
  summarise(TOTAL = sum(FV_WEIGHT)) |> 
  count() -> counts

df |> 
  filter(RIVERNAME_CLEANED == "TUSKET") |> 
  filter(YEAR %in% c(2020:2025)) |> 
  mutate(YEAR = as.factor(YEAR)) |>
  group_by(YEAR, LICENCE_ID) |> 
  summarise(TOTAL = sum(FV_WEIGHT)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = YEAR, y = TOTAL, fill = YEAR)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.8, outliers = FALSE) +
  geom_jitter(pch = 21, width = 0.1, alpha = 0.8) +
  #geom_point() +
  # geom_text(
  #   data = counts,
  #   aes(x = YEAR, y = -1, label = paste0("n=", n)),
  #   vjust = 0,
  #   inherit.aes = FALSE
  # ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    n.breaks = 10,
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Reported landings for Tusket",
    x = "",
    y = "Total landings per licence (kg)",
    fill = "Year"
    ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d()
```

```{r}
df |> 
  filter(RIVERNAME_CLEANED == "TUSKET") |> 
  filter(YEAR %in% c(2023, 2024, 2025)) |>
```

# Data - Age
```{r, warning=FALSE}
channel <- dbConnect(
  DBI::dbDriver("Oracle"),
  username = "GASPEREA",
  password = "_REMOVED",
  "PTRAN",
  believeNRows = FALSE
  )

dbListTables(channel)

# Get fish measurements for Tusket
fish_meas <- dbReadTable(channel, "ALOSA_FISH_BIO_DATA")
fish_meas |> 
  filter(SITE_ID == 2) -> fish_meas

# Get fish ages for Tusket
fish_age <- dbReadTable(channel, "ALOSA_FISH_AGE_DATA")
fish_age |> 
  # Get fish measured at Lake Vaughan only
  filter(SITE_ID == 2) -> fish_age

fish_age |> 
  left_join(fish_meas, by = c("YEAR", "FISH_ID")) |> 
  select(YEAR, CURRENT_AGE, AGE_AT_FIRST_SPAWN, MON, DAY, SPECIES_ID, SEX_ID, FORK_LENGTH, WEIGHT) |> 
  mutate(DATE = make_date(year = YEAR, month = MON, day = DAY), .after = YEAR) |> 
  select(-MON, -DAY) |> 
  filter(!(SEX_ID == 3)) |> 
  mutate(
    SEX_ID = case_when(
      SEX_ID == 1 ~ "M",
      SEX_ID == 2 ~ "F",
      TRUE ~ NA
      )
  ) -> fish_df
```

```{r}
# This takes the observations of species from the biocharacteristics data and 
# the supplementary observations (i.e. the ones just checking for species) and
# combines them to show how many BBs were actually observed for 2025
proportions <- split_species(
    year = 2025,
    siteID = 2,
    channel = channel
  )

# This shows the actual number of As and Bs we counted each day
proportions |>
  select(date, A, BB) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(A, BB), values_to = "observed", names_to = "species") |> 
  ggplot(aes(date, observed, fill = species)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge())

# This shows them as proportions
proportions |>
  select(date, A, BB) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(A, BB), values_to = "observed", names_to = "species") |> 
  ggplot(aes(date, observed, fill = species)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", alpha = 0.7, colour = "grey20") +

    title = "Species of fish measured at Lake Vaughan Dam in 2025",
    y = "Percentage",
    fill = "Species"
  ) +

      angle = 45,
      vjust = 1,
      hjust = 1
      ),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
```

```{r}
# This will show all the BBs we have estiamted across all years available
years <- c(2019:2025)
results_list <- list()

for (year in years) {
  
  temp_proportions <- split_species(
    year = year,
    siteID = 2,
    channel = channel
    )
  
  temp_df <- tryCatch(
    twospecies.river.escapement(
      filename = NULL,
      year = year,
      site = 2,
      channel = channel,
      species.split = temp_proportions
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      message("Year ", year, " not available. Skipping.")
      return(NULL)
    }
  )
  
  # skip if NULL or empty
  if (is.null(temp_df) || nrow(temp_df[[2]]) == 0) {
    message("No data for year ", year, ". Skipping.")
    next
  }
  
  bb_df <- temp_df[[2]]
  bb_df$year <- year
  bb_df$dayofyear <- as.integer(bb_df$dayofyear)
  results_list[[as.character(year)]] <- bb_df
  
}

all_years_df <- bind_rows(results_list)

all_years_df |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ ifelse(is.nan(.), 0, .))) |> 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ ifelse(is.na(.), 0, .))) |>  
  mutate(date = make_date(year = year, month = mon, day = day)) |> 
  mutate(year = as.factor(year)) |> 
  select(date, year, dayofyear, total, sd, clow, chigh) -> all_years_df

all_years_df |> 
  group_by(year) |> 
  summarise(total = sum(total), clow = sum(clow), chigh = sum(chigh)) -> all_years_BBs
  
all_years_BBs |> 
ggplot(aes(year, total)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = clow, ymax = chigh), width = 0.1) +
  geom_point(size = 2, pch = 21, fill = "grey30") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, n.breaks = 10) +
  labs(title = "Estimated escapement of bluebacks at Lake Vaughan Dam", subtitle = "Bars represent the 95% confidence interval", x = "", y = "Escapement") +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank())
```

# Reporting
```{r}
# New data from licencing
licences <- read_excel(path = "R:/Science/Population Ecology Division/DFD/Alosa/MARFISSCI/LA1040- Gaspereau Licences WITH SITE LOCATIONS 2024.xlsx", sheet = 1)

# Get all the licences that have ever reported for Tusket
df |> 
  #filter(YEAR %in% c(2020:2025)) |> 
  filter(RIVERNAME_CLEANED == "TUSKET") |> 
  distinct(LICENCE_ID, YEAR) |> 
  arrange(YEAR, LICENCE_ID) |> 
  select(YEAR, LICENCE_ID) |> 
  mutate(YEAR = as.factor(YEAR)) |> 
  mutate(REPORT_FLAG = "Y") -> tusket_fished

# Get all the licences that have ever reported DNF that appear in the list of 
# licences in the licences that have fished the tusket
didnotfish |> 
  filter(LICENCE_ID %in% tusket_fished$LICENCE_ID) |> 
  filter(NIL_REPORT_FLAG == "Y") -> tusket_dnf

# The following code creates a table that shows information we have on all licences
# that have ever reported catch or didnotfish on the Tusket since 2008. This 
# table will contian NAs where no information was recieved i.e. a "DNR" for 
# that year
tusket_fished |> 
  full_join(tusket_dnf) |> 
  # I am going to remove these records that have contradictory reporting for now
  # so we can get some estimate of licences fishing (n is only = 7).
  # Need to replace NA with N
  mutate(
    REPORT_FLAG = coalesce(REPORT_FLAG, "N"),
    NIL_REPORT_FLAG = coalesce(NIL_REPORT_FLAG, "N")
  ) |> 
  filter(!(REPORT_FLAG == "Y" & NIL_REPORT_FLAG == "Y")) |> 
  # Now that we have taken care of the instances where there were contradictory
  # entries, we can take one of these columns (they are the opposite of one
  # another) and use it to create a new column that shows us who reported
  select(YEAR, LICENCE_ID, REPORT_FLAG) |> 
  mutate(
    REPORT_FLAG = case_when(
      REPORT_FLAG == "N" ~ "DNF",
      TRUE ~ REPORT_FLAG
      )
  ) |> 
  # We need to add a function here (unique) to tell pivot_Wider to grab the first value
  # from the list as it creates a list when we have two character variables
  pivot_wider(names_from = YEAR, values_from = REPORT_FLAG, values_fn = unique) |> 
  arrange(LICENCE_ID) |> 
  mutate(
    across(everything(), ~ replace_na(., "DNR"))
  ) -> licence_table

#writexl::write_xlsx(licence_table, path = "C:/Users/graylo/Documents/tusket_reporting.xlsx")

# Make a plot showing the number of different responses for each year
licence_table |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -LICENCE_ID, names_to = "YEAR", values_to = "FISHED") |> 
  # mutate(FISHED = if_else(is.na(FISHED), "DNR", FISHED)) |> 
  # mutate(FISHED = if_else(FISHED == "N", "DNF", FISHED)) |> 
  mutate(FISHED = fct_relevel(FISHED, "DNR", "DNF", "Y")) |> 
  group_by(YEAR) |> 
  count(FISHED) |> 
  ggplot(aes(YEAR, n, fill = FISHED)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", alpha = 0.7, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_y_continuous(n.breaks = 10) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Reporting rates for licences on the Tusket River (as of ", paste(month(Sys.Date(), label = TRUE), year(Sys.Date())), ")"),
    #subtitle = "DNR = Did Not Report; DNF = Did Not Fish; Y = Reported",
    x = "",
    y = "Count",
    fill = "Reported?"
    ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1)
    ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d()  
```
